name: Drop cap
summary: A large first letter that drops down 2 or more lines of text and marks the start of a chapter or an article.
how: Set the drop cap to the height of 3 to 4 body lines; align its top with the cap height of the first line.
Set the first 3 to 5 words after it in small capitals.
Use one drop cap for each article or chapter.

origin.note: The Mainz Psalter of Fust and Schöffer prints large decorated initials in red and blue.

adoptions.via: Victorian books and magazines open chapters with engraved, ornamented initials.
Editorial sites open long articles with a large serif initial over 3 to 4 lines.

sources.title: Robert Bringhurst, The Elements of Typographic Style (1992)
